content: Sodium monofluorophosphate is an over-the-counter dental preparation that has been approved by the FDA for the prevention and treatment of dental cavities. It is commonly found in toothpaste formulations and is used to strengthen teeth and protect against decay. Adverse reactions that have been reported include flatulence and abdominal bloating. If more than the recommended amount for brushing is accidentally swallowed, it is advised to seek immediate medical attention or contact a Poison Control Center. The product is intended for oral use, and there is no specific FDA guidance on its use in various populations, including pregnant women, nursing mothers, pediatric patients, geriatric patients, or individuals with renal or hepatic impairment. Similarly, there is no specific guidance on its use in immunocompromised patients, individuals of different genders, or racial populations. The active ingredient in the product is sodium monofluorophosphate, which contains 0.76% sodium monofluorophosphate (equivalent to 0.15% w/v fluoride ion). Inactive ingredients include dicalcium phosphate dihydrate, water, glycerin, sodium lauryl sulfate, cellulose gum, flavoring agents, tetrasodium pyrophosphate, and sodium saccharin. The mechanism of action, pharmacodynamics, and pharmacokinetics of sodium monofluorophosphate are not well-documented in the drug label. Additionally, there is limited information regarding its nonclinical toxicology and clinical studies. The product is marketed under brand names such as Colgate® Fluoride Toothpaste, which is ADA (American Dental Association) accepted. It is available in various packaging, including an 85-gram tube labeled as Cavity Protection with active fluoride to strengthen teeth. Patients are advised to keep the product out of reach of children under six years of age. For any questions or comments, consumers can contact the toll-free number provided by the manufacturer. There is no established interaction between sodium monofluorophosphate and alcohol, but patients are encouraged to consult their healthcare provider regarding potential effects.
